chalisa.do1: Setting the beauty of the revered guru's lotus feet in the temple of my mind,
remembering Gajānana and Sarasvatī, and receiving the blessing of Śiva, the foe of Tripura,
chalisa.do2: know me for a witless man, a storehouse of faults;
I tell the fair fame of Paraśurāma as far as my understanding goes.
chalisa.cau1: Victory to Lord Paraśurāma, ocean of joy; victory to the lord of sages, a sun of virtue and knowledge.
chalisa.cau2: Crown of Bhṛgu's line, formidable and steadfast in battle, you have a kṣatriya's fire in your face and a saint's body.
chalisa.cau3: Son of Jamadagni, born of Reṇukā, your splendour and valour spread over the whole world.
chalisa.cau4: In the month of Vaiśākha, in the noble bright fortnight, on the third lunar day, under the charming Punarvasu,
chalisa.cau5: in the first watch of the night, when there was neither cold nor heat, on that day of bliss that spanned the dusk,
chalisa.cau6: then a baby cried in the sage's hut: Hari was born from Reṇukā's womb.
chalisa.cau7: Six planets stood exalted in their own houses, and Rāhu in Gemini stood firm in the fourth house, the house of happiness.
chalisa.cau8: Splendour and knowledge together took a human body; Brahman became incarnate in Jamadagni's house.
chalisa.cau9: The child was given the holy name Rāma; chanting that name, the world finds rest.
chalisa.cau10: On your forehead is the three-lined mark, and on your head lovely matted locks; on your shoulder is a charming sacred thread of muñja grass.
chalisa.cau11: A lovely girdle and a deerskin are at your waist; a fine rudrākṣa rosary is on your broad chest.
chalisa.cau12: Yellow garments grace your handsome body; the quiver and bow on your shoulder enchant the mind.
chalisa.cau13: You know the Vedas, the Purāṇas, śruti and smṛti; you are famed in the world as wrath embodied.
chalisa.cau14: In your right hand you raise the sacred axe, and in your left a Veda Saṃhitā looks lovely.
chalisa.cau15: You are learned, of boundless virtue and knowledge; you are master of both scripture and weapons.
chalisa.cau16: In the fourteen worlds and the nine regions of the earth, in all four directions, are your fair fame and fierce might.
chalisa.cau17: Once the sun to the lotus of Bhṛgu's line fought with Gaṇapati.
chalisa.cau18: Breaking his tusk, he brought the battle to a halt, and Gaṇapati came to be named Ekadanta, the one-tusked.
chalisa.cau19: There was a king, Kārtavīrya Arjuna, the thousand-armed, wicked and dreadful.
chalisa.cau20: Seeing the divine cow with Jamadagni, he resolved in his mind: I shall keep her in my own house.
chalisa.cau21: When she was not given to him for the asking, he fought; he was defeated, and the world laughed at him.
chalisa.cau22: A deep anger filled the wicked man's body and heart; his enmity towards the sage grew beyond measure.
chalisa.cau23: The great sage was absorbed in meditation; the king struck him with a spear.
chalisa.cau24: Struck by the spear, Jamadagni fell, as if the Creator had turned against the race of kṣatriyas.
chalisa.cau25: Hearing of his father's slaying and his mother's bitter weeping, he was seized with great anger, and boundless grief filled his mind.
chalisa.cau26: Taking the sharp, terrible axe in his hand, he slew the wicked one at once.
chalisa.cau27: With the blood of kṣatriyas he made the tarpaṇa offering to his father; the son took revenge for his father's slaying.
chalisa.cau28: Twenty-one times he rid the earth of kṣatriyas, and seizing the land, he gave it to the Brahmins.
chalisa.cau29: A lovely tale of the Tretā age: Śrī Rāma broke Śiva's bow.
chalisa.cau30: Knowing him for an enemy who had broken his guru's bow, Paraśurāma then resolved to destroy him root and all.
chalisa.cau31: Then Śrī Rāma, king of the Raghus, with folded hands made his humble entreaty, and then showed his power.
chalisa.cau32: Mighty Bhīṣma, Droṇa and Karṇa, and countless others in the Dvāpara age, became his disciples.
chalisa.cau33: By giving the science of weapons he earned fair fame; the guru's glory spread to every horizon.
chalisa.cau34: Through all four ages hosts of gods, sages, men and demons have sung your glory.
chalisa.cau35: Brother, he gave the wealth to Kaśyapa and went to Mount Mahendra to practise austerities.
chalisa.cau36: Lord, to this day you remain absorbed in samādhi; all the worlds ever bow their heads to you.
chalisa.cau37: You knew the four varṇas as one and equal; Lord, you are God, who sees all alike.
chalisa.cau38: In your refuge gods, demons, men, kings and beggars gain the four fruits of life.
chalisa.cau39: Whoever reads this Chālīsā of Śrī Paraśurāma, Śiva, Gaurī's lord, is ever gracious to him.
chalisa.cau40: Master, Lord who know every heart, dwell night and day in the heart of Pūrṇendu.
chalisa.do3: The lovely deeds of Paraśurāma wipe out all ignorance;
to one who has fallen at his refuge the Lord always gives fair fame and honour.
chalisa.shloka1: The sun of the line of divine Bhṛgu, the crusher of Sahasrabāhu,
the delight of Reṇukā's eyes, the treasure of the Brahmins: I bow to Paraśurāma.
